Formula (2.2) in the primary is missing its x factor; we do not use it. Connectivity means order at least l+1 and connected after deleting any set of fewer than l vertices. If someone adopts a weaker convention admitting smaller complete graphs, those extra complete graphs also have (1+x)^n and satisfy the conclusion, but the structural N>=1 parametrization is only for the standard domain.

Here is an independent complete structural audit. In a chordal graph every proper specified clique Q has a simplicial vertex outside Q. Induct on order. Complete graphs are immediate. Otherwise pick nonadjacent a,b and an inclusion-minimal a-b separator S; let A,B be their components after deleting S. Each s in S has a neighbour in both A and B, since otherwise S minus s still separates a,b. If s,t in S were nonadjacent, take a shortest s-t path with interiors in A, and one with interiors in B. Both are induced, have length at least two, and have no edges between their interiors. Their union is an induced cycle of length at least four, contradiction. Thus S is a clique. Q outside S lies in at most one component. Choose another nonempty component C (among A,B if necessary). The smaller induced chordal graph C union S has proper specified clique S, so induction gives a simplicial vertex in C. It has no neighbours outside C union S and is outside Q. If disconnected, S may be empty and the same argument applies. Base one-vertex graph and Q empty work; for empty graph there is no proper Q. This establishes the lemma without importing an unpaid chordal characterization.

Deleting a simplicial vertex v preserves l-connectivity whenever at least l+1 vertices remain: after deleting a further set S of size <l, paths between remaining vertices exist in G-S, and any occurrence of v with neighbours u,w is replaced by edge uw. A walk can be shortened to a path. Chordality and clique exclusion are inherited by induced subgraphs. Every current graph has minimum degree at least l: fewer neighbours could be deleted to isolate a vertex from another remaining vertex. At order l+1 every pair must be adjacent, since otherwise deleting the other l-1 vertices disconnects them. Thus successive simplicial deletions terminate at K_(l+1), not at an assumed arbitrary clique.

For a deleted vertex, its closed neighbourhood is a clique. K_(l+3)-freeness bounds its degree by l+1; minimum degree bounds it below by l. Let a,b be the numbers of degrees l,l+1 respectively. Then a,b>=0 and a+b=n-l-1. The clique recurrence follows from the bijection between cliques containing v and subsets of its clique neighbourhood: C(G)=C(G-v)+x(1+x)^deg(v). This includes the singleton v and all clique sizes, with no change to the empty coefficient. Telescoping gives C(G)=(1+x)^(l+1)+a x(1+x)^l+b x(1+x)^(l+1)=(1+x)^l(1+N x+b x²), with N=n-l=a+b+1>=1 and 0<=b<=N-1. For b=0, the remaining factor is linear with root -1/N. For b>0, discriminant N²-4b >= (N-2)² >=0, so the quadratic splits over the reals, including repeated roots. Multiplication adds only -1 roots. Boundary cases: terminal K_(l+1) has N=1,b=a=0; complete K_(l+2) has N=2,b=1,a=0 and quadratic (1+x)². No larger complete graph is allowed. l=1 gives the connected K4-free theorem; l=2 is included without an additional assumption. All orders and all positive l are covered.
